correctness.rationale: For n>=4, spoke length t in [1/2,1], rim edges 1, the weighted graph geodesic has hub-rim=t, adjacent rim=1 and other rim=2t. On the zero-sum space the powered distance quadratic form splits exactly into radial coefficient F_n=2+(n-3)(2t)^p-2n*t^p and rim Fourier eigenvalues -b+(1-b)*2*cos(2pi*k/n). The greatest rim eigenvalue is (2c_n-1)b-2c_n, with real multiplicity 1 (even n) or 2 (odd n). Radial F_n strictly increases in p and has exactly one zero >1; its zero increases in t while the rim threshold log(b_n)/log(2t) decreases. These give one simultaneous crossing and the stated closed formulas b_n=2c_n/(2c_n-1), s_n=[2+(n-3)b_n]/(2n), p*=log_2(b_n/s_n), t*=s_n^(1/p*). Nullity 2/3 at crossing, hence centered Schoenberg Gram rank n-2/n-3. Independent shortest-distance and centered-Gram calculations for n=4,5,6,7,11 corroborated both parity nullities, but are not proof for all n and t.
